headline: Highest risk is broad network egress plus REST API use creating data-leak and cascading-error pathways; prompt-injection and compliance risks are otherwise limited by sparse evidence.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel or file bridge is documented, so direct prompt injection between nuwa-skill and opik is not evidenced. However, opik exposes a REST API and nuwa-skill has allowlisted network egress, so an unusual integration could pass attacker-controlled text. The pathway is plausible but not default.
conditions: IF nuwa-skill is configured to send outputs into opik via REST payloads, injection becomes plausible.
IF either agent begins parsing the other's text as instructions, the risk increases.
mitigations: Keep the agents disconnected except for typed, schema-validated fields.
Strip instruction-like text from any payload before forwarding.
Use a fixed JSON schema for inter-agent messages.
Review any REST integration for prompt delimiters.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags and content filtering at the bridge.

B_data_leakage.rationale: nuwa-skill has allowlisted network egress and opik has broad egress plus REST API calls, so either agent can transmit data off-box in default configurations. No sensitive data classes are listed, so the blast radius is inferred as moderate rather than high. The pairwise leakage pathway exists through networked outputs even though direct shared storage is not documented.
conditions: IF either agent is given secrets, logs, or user content, that content can be transmitted over network egress.
IF opik is connected to an external REST endpoint, its outputs may leave the local environment.
mitigations: Do not route secrets or private documents through either agent.
Restrict opik REST endpoints to trusted hosts only.
Disable outbound egress except for explicit allowlists.
Redact logs before any API call.
requires-engineering: add DLP checks on outbound payloads.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have network-facing capabilities, but only opik explicitly calls REST APIs and nuwa-skill only shows allowlisted egress. There is no evidence of shared filesystem, git, or overlapping mutable scopes, so write-write conflict is not documented. Uncertainty remains, but the safer reading is a limited conflict risk.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable REST-backed resource, conflicts can occur.
IF an orchestrator gives both agents write access to the same endpoint, contention becomes likely.
mitigations: Assign separate API credentials per agent.
Serialize writes through one coordinator.
Use idempotent REST operations where possible.
Add request IDs to detect duplicate updates.
requires-engineering: implement locking or optimistic concurrency.

D_cascading_error.rationale: opik is an evaluation/observability tool, so it may render or act on nuwa-skill outputs, but no verification or guardrail is documented. Because nuwa-skill is scientific-research oriented and opik exposes REST APIs, a bad output could be propagated downstream. The interaction is inferred, not directly evidenced, so medium is the conservative choice.
conditions: IF opik consumes nuwa-skill outputs as evaluation inputs without verification, errors can cascade.
IF opik triggers downstream automation from those outputs, the blast radius increases.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before acting on outputs.
Require schema validation on nuwa-skill outputs.
Compare outputs against a second source before use.
Log provenance for every forwarded field.
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented for either nuwa-skill or opik. Both profiles are open-source and list no data classes touched, so a compliance breach pathway is not evidenced. The other agent is not separately implicated because the relevant compliance fields are absent for both.
conditions: IF future deployments route regulated data through either agent, compliance review is required.
IF either profile later documents residency or retention constraints, reassess this verdict.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents.
Document data handling before deployment.
Review retention settings in any wrapper service.
Confirm hosting region for any external API.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated data.
